h1: Charoen Hotel — Long-Running City-Center Hotel on Pho Si Road, Near the Train Station, Udon Thani
intro: Mention city-center hotels in Udon to older locals and one of the first names many will think of is Charoen Hotel — a long-running hotel on Pho Si Road that has been part of the city since 1969 and went through a major renovation in 2015 · Its main draw is a central location within walking distance of Central Plaza and UD Town, about 1 km from the train station, plus a garden-side pool, three restaurants, and a large banquet hall that has hosted countless Udon weddings and seminars · 213 rooms, from about THB 900/night · scored 8.5 from real reviews.

body.html: Who Charoen Hotel suits — to put it as simply as possible, Charoen Hotel is the long-running city hotel of Udon that sells location and value above newness or modern design · It has been open since 1969 and had a major renovation in 2015, with 213 rooms and suites total. It sits on Pho Si Road in Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani district — a city-center commercial area that stays busy all day · From real reviews across several platforms, the people it suits best are travelers who want to stay in the city center at an affordable price, people in town on business or for work, families who want a larger room with a pool for the kids, and anyone connecting by train or heading on to Nong Khai-Vientiane, since it's close to the train station · On the other hand, if you're after a brand-new boutique hotel with flawless rooms in every corner, or the quiet of a suburban resort, this may not be the answer, because the appeal of Charoen Hotel lies in being a classic city-center hotel that has been part of Udon for a long time · To be clear, it's a hotel where "the legend lives on" and still does its job as a well-located place to stay at a price many are happy with, even if the building has been through several decades of wear.

Location and getting around — this is Charoen Hotel's biggest strength, no question · The hotel sits in the middle of the commercial district on Pho Si Road, which many reviews rate very highly for location (TripAdvisor gives the location category around 4.1 out of 5, and Trip.com scores location as high as 9.1) · The interesting part is that you can walk to Central Plaza Udon Thani and UD Town in about 7-10 minutes, so you don't have to rely on a car all the time — step out of the lobby and you can walk to food, shopping, and a movie · The area around the hotel is also packed with restaurants, cafes, and local shops within walking distance · Getting around further afield is convenient too: Udon Thani train station is only about 1 km away, which is ideal for people arriving by train or continuing on to Nong Khai, while Udon Thani Airport (UTH) is about 6 km away, roughly a 10-15 min drive · Nong Prajak Park and the city's well-known markets are also a short drive away · One thing worth knowing is that Pho Si Road is a busy commercial street with traffic and noise throughout the day, so rooms facing the street or on lower floors will clearly hear the noise from outside — something to factor in when choosing a room.

"Great location, easy walk to Central and UD Town, lots of food around, and the staff are lovely and helpful · The renovated rooms are clean and roomier than expected, really good value for a city-center hotel in Udon."

Room types and decor — Charoen Hotel has 213 rooms and suites total across several tiers, from Deluxe Double and Deluxe Twin for couples and general travelers up to Family Suite for families and the Royal Suite, the hotel's largest room · The thing to say plainly from the start is that room quality here isn't the same across the board, because it's an older building that's been partly renovated · The renovated rooms get plenty of praise for being clean, spacious, with comfortable beds and a full set of amenities — many reviews say they're roomier than what you pay · But rooms that haven't been renovated clearly look older, with reviews mentioning well-worn furniture, showerheads mounted quite low, and beds that are fairly firm in some rooms · The simple takeaway is that if you book here, you should request a renovated room at the time of booking or check-in — it makes a big difference to the experience · One point many agree on, whatever the room, is the fast and stable Wi-Fi, which is a plus for anyone here to work · Overall the decor is classic-hotel style in warm tones, nothing flashy like a new boutique, but it feels like a hotel that genuinely works and has a lot of space in the room — something that's getting harder to find in newer hotels, which often design rooms to be compact.

Facilities, pool, and gym — for a hotel in this price range, Charoen Hotel has more facilities on offer than the typical city hotel · The highlight is the outdoor pool set beside a small garden within the hotel, which makes the area around the pool shady and quieter than the street side. Many reviews praise the pool as a good spot to relax, especially in the late morning and evening, and kids can swim comfortably · Beyond the pool there's a gym, three restaurants, a bar, karaoke, and a discotheque for anyone who wants some nighttime entertainment without going far · What sets Charoen Hotel apart from others in town is its large banquet and meeting halls that seat up to around 1,500 people, which has made it a popular venue for weddings, parties, and seminars in Udon for decades · There's free parking, free Wi-Fi in all rooms, daily housekeeping, and 24-hour security and front desk · To be honest, some of the facilities are starting to show their age along with the building — the gym equipment and some common areas look a bit dated — but in terms of variety and real usability it does well for this price range.

Food and bar — the hotel has three restaurants and an in-house bar, covering both main meals and dinner · Breakfast is a buffet included in many room packages, with Thai, Chinese, and international options to choose from · Breakfast is where opinions split quite a bit — some reviews say it's filling and offers enough choice for the price, but plenty of voices complain that the breakfast menu is fairly repetitive day to day and some items aren't as fresh and hot as they should be, such as eggs prepared in advance · The upside of the location is that if you tire of the hotel food, just a few minutes' walk gets you to plenty of Udon's restaurants and cafes, plus the options inside Central and UD Town within walking distance, so you don't have to rely on the hotel restaurants for every meal · As for the bar, karaoke, and discotheque, they're a draw for people who enjoy nighttime entertainment, but they're a double-edged sword, since noise can sometimes carry to rooms near that zone on certain nights — if you're sensitive to noise, ask for a room further away · In short, the food at Charoen Hotel is fine and convenient as a backup option, but it's not the reason you'd come here to eat in the hotel.

Service — service is another point that draws fairly consistent praise in real reviews · The words that come up again are staff being "friendly," "helpful," and "attentive," especially the front-desk team, which many reviews say responds quickly, is cheerful, and handles on-the-spot problems well · Trip.com scores service around 8.5 and TripAdvisor around 3.9 out of 5, which is solid for a hotel at this level · Being a long-running hotel in town, many of the staff have worked here for years and are used to looking after both Thai and international guests · But to be straight, there are a few voices noting that care and cleaning aren't equally consistent every day, and that some staff have limited English — common enough at local hotels · Overall, service remains a strength that helps make up for the age of the building to a fair degree.

What real reviews say (praise and criticism) — pulling together Trip.com, Agoda, Booking.com, and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the city-center location within walking distance of Central and UD Town, being close to the train station and handy for connections, friendly and helpful staff, renovated rooms that are clean and spacious, the garden-side pool with its shady setting, fast Wi-Fi, and good value that brings customers back · On the watch-out side: the most talked-about issue is noise — the hotel sits on a busy commercial street, with some reviews going as far as writing "VERY NOISY" and saying the windows don't block sound well · Next is the age of the building, which many describe as "a faded beauty," even after the renovation · Then there's the repetitive breakfast, uneven room quality, low-mounted showerheads, and firm beds in some rooms · Most of these criticisms are things you can manage by choosing your room well and setting the right expectations, rather than problems that keep people from coming back.

"The renovated rooms are nicely clean, the pool is shady and pleasant to relax by, and the price is cheap for the location · The only downside is the street noise is fairly loud in rooms facing the road — next time I'll ask for an inner room by the pool instead."

Price and value — the starting rate for a standard room is about THB 900/night at regular prices (some promotional periods drop below that), rising to around THB 1,200-1,600 for the larger deluxe rooms, while suites like the Family Suite and Royal Suite are in the range of around THB 2,000 and up · Compared with other city hotels in Udon, Charoen Hotel falls into the good value for location group — you get a place to stay in the city center within walking distance of the big malls and close to the train station, plus a pool and several facilities, at a price close to a typical mid-range hotel · Measured by location per baht, it does well, and that's the main reason people choose to stay · But measured by newness and the polish of the rooms, newer boutique hotels in town at a similar price may offer rooms in better condition, so the value of Charoen Hotel comes down to whether you weight "location and space" or "newness of the room" more heavily.

What to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · One, request a renovated room at the time of booking or check-in, because room quality here isn't the same and updated rooms are clearly different from the older ones · Two, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a higher floor and a side that doesn't face Pho Si Road, or the side by the pool, since the street out front is busy all day · Three, check the transport details — the hotel emphasizes that it's close to the train station (about 1 km), but some sources note there's no free airport shuttle and there may be a charge for a train-station transfer, so confirm with the front desk first if you need it · Four, compare the room-only rate against the rate with breakfast, since opinions on breakfast are split and some may prefer to eat out where there's more choice · Five, during big weddings or banquets in the ballroom, the hotel can get lively and crowded, so ask ahead if you want quiet · Six, choose free cancellation if your plans aren't set, since prices change with the dates.

Bottom line — from all the real reviews, Charoen Hotel is the best fit for people who want to stay in central Udon at an affordable price, walk to Central and UD Town, be near the train station, and have a larger room with a pool · Its appeal is being a classic hotel that has been part of the city for more than half a century, with a wide range of facilities and a location that's hard to match · But you do have to accept that the building is old, room quality is uneven, and street noise is something you'll need to plan around · If you're looking for a new hotel with polished design or full quiet, this may not be it, and you should consider a newer boutique hotel in town instead · But for people who value location, space in the room, and value for money — and are willing to pick a renovated room and handle the noise — Charoen Hotel is still a city-center option in Udon that's comfortable to stay in at a price many are happy with, and the reason the name is still on the minds of travelers coming to Udon to this day.

honestSummary: Charoen Hotel is the best fit for people who want to stay in central Udon at an affordable price, walk to Central and UD Town, be near the train station, and have a larger room with a pool · But you have to accept it's a long-running hotel over half a century old; the building and some rooms are getting old, room quality is uneven, and it sits on a noisy commercial street, so you need to pick a renovated room and handle the noise well.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Charoen Hotel Udon Thani

faq.q: Where is Charoen Hotel, and what can you walk to?
faq.a: Charoen Hotel is located at 549-559 Pho Si Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani district, in the city center · It's about a 7-10 minute walk to Central Plaza and UD Town · It's close to Udon Thani train station (about 1 km) and about 6 km from Udon Thani Airport (a 10-15 min drive) · The area around it is full of restaurants and shops in the commercial district.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Charoen Hotel, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 900/night for a standard room · There's the Deluxe Double, Deluxe Twin, Family Suite, and Royal Suite for families and groups · Prices rise during high season and on days with events in town, so compare several platforms before booking and request a renovated room.

faq.q: What pool and facilities does Charoen Hotel have?
faq.a: It has an outdoor garden-side pool, a gym, 3 restaurants, a bar, karaoke, and a large banquet hall that seats up to around 1,500 people · There's free parking and free Wi-Fi in all rooms · The pool sits beside the garden, making it shady and quieter than the street side, good for relaxing in the late morning and evening.

faq.q: Is Charoen Hotel old, and what condition are the rooms in?
faq.a: The hotel has been open since 1969 and was renovated in 2015 · Room quality is uneven; renovated rooms are clean and spacious, but rooms that haven't been updated look older, with reviews mentioning low-mounted showerheads and fairly firm beds in some rooms · We recommend requesting a renovated room on a higher floor at the time of booking.

faq.q: Is Charoen Hotel noisy, and what kind of room should you request?
faq.a: Many reviews agree the hotel sits on Pho Si Road, which is busy all day, and rooms facing the road or on lower floors clearly hear traffic noise — some reviews even write that it's very noisy · If you're a light sleeper, we recommend requesting a higher floor and a side that doesn't face the road, or the side by the pool, at booking or check-in.

faq.q: Who is Charoen Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people who want to stay in central Udon at an affordable price, walk to Central and UD Town, be near the train station, and have a larger room with a pool · It suits budget travelers, people on business, families, and anyone arriving by train or heading on to Nong Khai-Vientiane · If you're looking for a new hotel with polished design or full quiet, a newer boutique hotel in town may suit you better.
